O4.text: A second response shape on the same URL selected by a header is a known cache hazard. Next.js adds an `_rsc` search param to every router request "for CDNs that don't support custom headers... rather than relying on Vary", and htmx users get the fragment on reopen-tab and reload (issues 724, 497). Brumate already varies on x-brumate-base; Q1 B (private) avoids shared caches but not the browser history cache, and it removes any CDN hit for navigation responses. Likelihood medium; the fix is option C (a separate URL), which is a larger change than P1 states.

O12.text: The dedupe script blanks any long state string whose text is in the HTML; it does not check that resume never reads it. In DocPage.brm the loop `#for (part, index of page.parts by index)` renders `{part.html}` from `page = pages[slug]`, and `slug` is a prop. State records exist so the browser can re-run a block (a changed prop, `#key`, a `#loading` reload, a refresh), and a block that re-runs with "" would render empty prose. A safe dedupe needs the compiler to prove that the value only reaches a one-time raw insert whose DOM is already there, or the client must read it back from the DOM, whose serialization differs from the string (entities, attribute order). That is a compiler analysis, larger than the M node P7 and P10 assume. Likelihood of a silent blank render without it: high for any page that updates a prop.

evidence.source: website/src/components/DocPage.brm lines 12-17 and 112-139; docs/decisions.md line 142 (blocks re-run on update); evidence/dedupe-state.mjs strips by substring match only

O13.text: A constant marker query parameter does not cure O4. The partial body depends on x-brumate-keep and x-brumate-base, so two clients at the same marker URL need different bodies, and a CDN that drops Vary stores the first. Next.js knows this: its `_rsc` value is a hash of the prefetch, segment-prefetch, router-state-tree and next-url headers. A hashed parameter makes a URL per client state, which is a shared cache that never hits, the same result as Q1 B (private). So the marker only adds URL churn and a strip step in the server; the safety comes from `cache-control: private`, and the history-cache case is covered only if the marker is in the URL of every partial fetch.

evidence.detail: computeCacheBustingSearchParam takes the prefetch, segment prefetch, state tree and url headers

A real partial must renumber or resend, and the client must keep its layouts' state (assumed by P8). P12.text: Frame the dedupe spike as a server-side serialization choice with a test, not a compiler proof and not a client read-back. The server writes the state, so it can mark a long string that its own markup already printed (the raw html of an insert) and leave it out of the record. The spike's first question is the one O12 raised: does any re-run read such a string? Evidence from the code: the docs page is `<DocPage slug=(params.page) />` and DocPage reads `pages[slug]` of a module, so a prop change there can only be a navigation. The spike must prove that case against the key rule of `plan` (navigate.ts:123), which pairs routes by slot name and key: if a changed param gives a new key the region is replaced and its new state runs, and nothing re-runs with the blank. It stays an unknown until measured. Exit: a test that changes the prop, `#key`, a `#loading` reload and a refresh on a blanked page and renders the same HTML, else no-go and the full swap stays as it is.

evidence.source: docs/debates/navigation/evidence/partial-measure-outcome.md (harness flags, no throttle in the baseline)
evidence.detail: the harness runs without network or CPU throttle; throttle is a Chrome setting, not a code change
